description: WO-G4: Blender takes its place beside ComfyUI and Kohya_ss — a view-toggle button, a container, and the same enabled-gating. No new interaction concept, because a new concept is new friction and the user already knows this shape.

assert.note: the tab's existence comes from a MEASUREMENT of this machine, not from a default — a renderer-local stub could not know this pid
measuring starts a headless Blender, so it is a button rather than something that happens on open — see finding E3-2, half a minute on aarch64 under qemu
🔴 a panel that filled in a plausible version number would pass every assertion anyone would think to write, and be a lie
the same classes ComfyUI and Kohya use when their app is not answering — no new interaction concept

⚑ THE ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE PATTERN, ASSERTED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. Blender is a native application: there is no URL to embed. A <webview> here would mean someone had pointed the tab at something that is not Blender.
WO-G6. BAT rewrites .blend files with Blender closed and is not an add-on, so nothing we baseline can see it. The app hosts it instead of trying to detect it.
the same shape as the tab bar above it, one level down — not a new concept

auditNote:
The gate script owns the two assertions a single boot cannot make.

(1) ABSENT, NOT GREYED. With no Blender on the machine the tab must have NO NODE and the string `data-view="blender"` must not appear in the serialised document at all. That needs a second boot with SCRUPLE_BLENDER_BIN cleared and the vendor path pointed at an empty directory — the same mutation WO-E5's `blender-absent` scenario uses.

(2) THE OTHER TABS ARE UNCHANGED, ASSERTED BY DIFF, NOT BY EYE. The gate compares the tab set with Blender present against the tab set with Blender absent: the difference must be EXACTLY the Blender button and nothing else. An eye comparing two screenshots is how a missing tab survives seven work orders.
